## Problem

A model is deployed and somebody upstream asks the assurance
question: is it fair, is it robust, and can you show the numbers you
will be compared against later? Without a recorded baseline there is
no regression to detect, no evidence to hand an auditor, and no way
to tell drift from noise. The manifest dedicates Layer DEFENCE's
d-03-assurance-evals-benchmarks to exactly this stack — lm-eval-harness
(the standard few-shot benchmark runner), deepeval (unit-test-style
LLM metrics), robustbench (standardized adversarial robustness), giskard
(eval/scan for LLM agents), fairlearn and aif360 (fairness metrics and
mitigation) — and d-07 is where the results must land as
standards evidence.

## Solution

Fix three decisions first — metrics, dataset, threshold policy —
then run the baselines and record them where the verifier can find
them:

```bash
# 1. What the manifest declares for the D-3 surface
kailash list --category d-03-assurance-evals-benchmarks
kailash info fairlearn        # -> DEFENCE / d-03, bespoke deriv, safe

# 2. Standard benchmark surface (the comparable, public part):
lm_eval --model hf \
    --model_args pretrained=<your-model-or-rev> \
    --tasks <standard-tasks> \
    --device cuda:0 \
    --batch_size 8 \
    --output_path /srv/evals/<model>/<date>/

# 3. Unit-test-style LLM metrics (pytest-shaped, LLM-as-judge where the
#    metric needs one):
deepeval test run /srv/evals/<model>/test_baseline.py
#    test_baseline.py: assert_test(case, metrics=[BiasMetric(...)]) shape

# 4. Fairness metrics — group-conditioned, over a declared sensitive
#    feature (python; the MetricFrame shape from fairlearn's docs):
#    mf = MetricFrame(metrics=<sklearn metric>, y_true=..., y_pred=...,
#                     sensitive_features=...)
#    mf.overall / mf.by_group
#    aif360: dataset + model metrics over BinaryLabelDataset for the
#    comprehensive metric set (both stacks are importable, not CLIs)

# 5. Adversarial robustness baseline (vision-class models; the model
#    zoo + attack suite are the benchmark):
#    from robustbench.utils import load_model
#    model = load_model(model_name=<name>, dataset=<ds>,
#                       threat_model=<Linf|L2|corruptions>)
#    -> load a zoo model / your own candidate, evaluate robust
#       accuracy under the suite's attacks

# 6. Whole-system scan for the agentic/LLM-app surface (giskard v3
#    shape; provider key required for the judge):
#    from giskard.scan import vulnerability_scan
#    await vulnerability_scan(target=<your-agent>,
#        description="<system description>", languages=["en"])

# 7. RECORD the baseline: one file per model per window, with the
#    tool versions (the lock), the dataset rev, the metric list, the
#    thresholds, and the numbers — machine-readable first
kailash manifest validate     # the build half of the evidence
```

Expected output shape (abridged, shapes not transcripts):

```
baseline record (JSON):
{
  "model": "<id>@<rev>", "date": "<window>",
  "tools": {"lm-eval-harness": "<pin>", "deepeval": "<pin>",
            "fairlearn": "<pin>", ...},
  "benchmarks": {"<task>": {"metric": <float>, "n": <int>}},
  "fairness": {"<metric>": {"overall": <float>,
                 "by_group": {"<group>": <float>, ...}}},
  "robustness": {"<dataset/threat_model>": {"robust_acc": <float>}},
  "thresholds": {"<metric>": {"floor": <float>, "action": "<on-breach>"}},
  "evidence_ref": "<d-07 mapping for this record>"
}
```

The threshold policy — the part that makes a baseline actionable —
is declared, per metric, in the record itself: a floor value, and the
action on breach (`block-release`, `open-review`, `investigate`).
Breach testing is then mechanical:

```bash
# every subsequent window re-runs the SAME commands under the SAME
# dataset revs; a diff against the baseline record is the regression
# report — threshold breaches are visible by inspection, no vibes
```

## Discussion

- **Metrics choice is a decision, not a default.** Fairlearn's own
  guidance notes common fairness metrics (demographic parity,
  equalized odds, the four-fifths rule) each carry assumptions and
  construct-validity questions — the choice is a domain decision to
  be documented, not picked by convention. The practical shape:
  name the sensitive feature(s), pick the constraint family, record
  WHY in the baseline file. MetricFrame gives per-group
  decomposition of any sklearn metric; AIF360 adds the
  dataset-level metrics and the mitigation algorithms when the
  baseline fails its floor. Fairness runs are import-shaped (both
  are libraries, not CLIs) — the recipe's commands are the
  invocation context, the libraries' APIs are the surface.
- **Robustness baselines belong to a threat model, not a feeling:**
  robustbench standardises dataset + threat model (Linf / L2 /
  corruptions) + model zoo; a number without those three names is
  not comparable to anything, least of all to next quarter's run.
  For vision-class deployments this is the standard; for LLM-class
  deployments the robustness question moves to the harness/scan
  rows (lm-eval adversarial task families, deepeval/red-team style
  suites, giskard's vulnerability scan).
- **The LLM half of the assurance picture:** lm-eval-harness gives
  the public, comparable few-shot benchmark surface (`--tasks`,
  `--model_args pretrained=…,revision=…` — the revision flag is how
  you pin WHICH checkpoint you measured); deepeval wraps LLM metrics
  as pytest tests (`deepeval test run`, `assert_test` with metric
  instances — bias among the metric families the manifest maps);
  giskard's v3 surface is the async agent-level
  `vulnerability_scan`/`quality_scan` pair (v2's `giskard.scan` API
  remains available but unmaintained — pin-era note recorded in the
  provenance footer).
- **How it feeds standards evidence (d-07):** d-07's toolset is data
  packs + the `kailash-verifier` CLI (`kailash verifier --standard
  aisvs --level N` — renders per-tool standards evidence FROM the
  manifest, spec §3.8; the verifier and the
  aisvs-1.0-toolkit / mlsvs-toolkit / llm-top10-toolkit data packs are
  planned first-party deliverables). The contract this recipe feeds:
  the baseline record's `evidence_ref` names the standard + level the
  record supports, so the verifier renders the matrix and the record
  IS the per-tool evidence — no re-narration, no hand-written audit
  story. Until the verifier lands, the record plus the manifest
  citations is the explicit PENDING state, pointed at the d-07 rows.
- **All six rows are `safe`:** every D-3 row carries
  `safety.level: safe` — no live firing; the scan/eval targets are
  your own model endpoint or the bench suite's own data. What is NOT
  free is the provider key for judge-style metrics: it lives at
  `~/.config/kailash/keys/` per the OS secrets posture, never in the
  store or the repo.
- **Dataset revs are part of the evidence:** a benchmark number is a
  fact only relative to the dataset revision it ran on — record the
  rev (the same lock discipline the tool pins use) or the eventual
  diff is ambiguous between model drift and data drift.
- **When the baseline fails:** the threshold policy's `action` is the
  pre-agreed answer. fairness floors breach → mitigation (fairlearn
  reductions / aif360 algorithms) is the next recipe in this lane;
  robustness floors breach → the A-5 attack stack (ART/foolbox-class)
  is the diagnostic lane. Baseline → mitigation is a loop, not a
  one-shot.
